system_overview: This specification models the voucher transfer operation from RFC 3506, implemented using the Two-Phase Commit protocol. A Voucher Transaction Provider coordinates the transfer of vouchers between two types of holders: source holders (current owners) and destination holders (future owners). The transfer operation changes voucher ownership without altering the voucher's lifecycle state.
actors_and_components: Four types of participants interact: (1) A Voucher Transaction Provider (the coordinator) managing the commit/abort decision. (2) Source Voucher Holders who currently own the vouchers and wish to transfer them. (3) Destination Voucher Holders who are waiting to receive the vouchers. (4) The vouchers themselves, which remain in the valid state throughout the transfer. Communication uses a shared message pool.
state_variables: The system tracks seven pieces of state: (1) each voucher's current status (always valid during a transfer), (2) each voucher's lifecycle phase (always working during a transfer), (3) each source holder's participation state (holding, prepared, transferred, or aborted), (4) each destination holder's participation state (waiting, prepared, holding, or aborted), (5) the coordinator's state (initial or done), (6) the set of participants from which the coordinator has received transfer preparation confirmations, and (7) the pool of all messages sent.
initial_state: All vouchers are in the valid state with lifecycle in the working phase. All source holders are in the holding state. All destination holders are in the waiting state. The coordinator is in the initial state with empty preparation confirmations and empty message pool.
actions: The coordinator can: receive preparation confirmations from a source holder and a destination holder, execute a transfer (broadcasting a transfer message, enabled only when all participants have prepared), or spontaneously abort. Each source holder can: prepare for transfer (sending a preparation message), spontaneously abort, receive a transfer message (transitioning to the transferred state), or receive an abort message. Each destination holder can: prepare, spontaneously abort, receive a transfer message (transitioning to the holding state, indicating they now own the voucher), or receive an abort message.
safety_properties: Type correctness ensures all variables remain in expected domains. A consistency invariant ensures no source holder and destination holder reach conflicting decisions: a source holder must not be in the transferred state while a destination holder is aborted, and a source holder must not be aborted while a destination holder is in the holding state.
model_bounds: The model-checking configuration uses three vouchers, three source holders, and three destination holders. Deadlock checking is disabled.
additional_assumptions: The specification imports and claims to implement the voucher lifecycle specification as a refinement. The RFC does not distinguish between source and destination holders, but the specification introduces this distinction for clarity. Unlike other voucher operations, transfer does not change the voucher's status or lifecycle state; it only changes the holder identity, which is not explicitly tracked in this specification. Messages accumulate in a set and are never consumed.
